utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Good afternoon, everyone. There are a few matters I wish to deal with before we continue to hear the witness's evidence. That's why we started in open session. The first matter relates to the motion for a videolink testimony. Mr. Tieger, we haven't received any indication that additional information in relation to Mr. Asim Egrlic's testimony via videolink has been filed or will be soon filed. So could you give us an update as to where we stand in this regard?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. At this point, we do not anticipate the submission of further documentation related to the motion for videolink. Obviously we would keep the Court apprised if that would change. That would mean that the Prosecution would need to move forward on scheduling the witness for his appearance in the normal fashion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. For the next matter, may the Chamber move into private session briefly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Next, the Chamber will issue an oral ruling regarding the admissibility of 65 ter 40199, a video from 1995 that the Prosecution sought to tender through Witness KDZ-379 on 15 September 2011. The accused's legal adviser objects to the admission of those excerpts which contain the statements of Miroslav Stanic and date from April 1995, arguing that these portions of the interview contained extra contemporaneous statements of a third party. The Defence argues that in May 2010, the Chamber had denied the admission into evidence of a video interview that the accused had shown to a witness in very similar circumstances. The Prosecution submits in response, inter alia, that the video is admissible because it is relevant and probative and because the Prosecution demonstrated a nexus between the witness, KDZ-379, and the video proposed for admission. Having reviewed the submissions, the Chamber is of the view that the video is admissible pursuant to Rule 89(C). As the Prosecution correctly notes, the video is relevant and probative with regard to the circumstances surrounding the takeover of Foca municipality in April 1992. The witness also confirmed multiple parts of the video including the identity of the interviewee, Miroslav Stanic and commented on some of the statements Stanic made in the video about SDS policies in Foca municipalities. The Chamber also notes that the Defence arguments regarding the May 2010 video evidence is in error. On 6 May 2010, the Chamber by majority, myself dissenting, admitted the video clips containing interviews of third party that the accused had tendered for admission into evidence as Exhibits D130 and D133. The Chamber therefore orders that 65 ter 40199 be admitted into evidence and assigned an exhibit number. That can be done right now.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, that would be Exhibit P3476.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Unless there are matters to be dealt with in open session, we will go into closed session and continue the previous evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, I'm being asked by the court deputy as to when we will be hearing the evidence of Mr. Dzafic. Are we in a position to estimate, albeit roughly?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, my understanding is that based upon consultations with the Registry and assessments of the witness schedule, that it's everyone's assessment at this point that he would -- the videolink would take place on Friday. I believe that's a shared view. That's the basis upon which we have been operating, at least from this morning forward, and I have no reason to think that's likely to change based on the best estimates we have of the current witness schedule.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: What is the estimated time for your examination-in-chief, if you could remind me of it?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: One half hour, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And one hour, I was told. And for the cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: I don't believe we received a time yet from the Chamber for cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We will come back to the issue in the meantime. In the meantime let us go -- yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Just double-checked that, Mr. President and your understanding was correct. It is currently listed at one hour. That's right. I'm happy to double-check to see if that's changed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. We will come back to that scheduling issue later on. We will go into closed session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are now in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Tieger, I wonder whether you can address us in relation to the motion I referred to.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, I believe I can. I will bear in mind that we are in open session. Should be there any need - I don't anticipate one at the moment - to go into private session --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: -- I will ask to do so. Otherwise, I may be a little elliptical in making some reference but I trust the Court will let me know if it's not understood. The Prosecution's position, Mr. President, is there is no basis, no need, for the remedy sought by the Defence, and, indeed, to do so would work a quite unfair hardship on the witness and on the trial schedule generally. Let me address the issue of need first. I'm holding in my hand the transcript in question. It's not 122 pages, it's 105 pages. It looks like this, this kind of printing. The length of time that it would take to review this transcript is relatively minimal. I have no idea why no member of the Defence team attempted to do so in the six days that have passed between the receipt of this document and now. Or whether some member of the Defence team did and it has not been noted in the motion but a relatively short period of time would be required to do so. Which brings me to the second point. There is still more than sufficient time for review of the transcript and any related materials before the testimony of the witness. Third point would simply be that there is no basis for the motion, the suggestion that the relationship between the position of the witness whose materials have recently been disclosed and the witness about to testify gives rise to some particular need to do so is purely speculative. Indeed, on the face of those two different positions I would suggest that the contrary and my quick look at the transcript indeed revealed at least one or two references that confirmed that impression. But the main point is that it is entirely speculative at the moment and there is no basis for the assertion that detailed analysis is necessary. Fourth, the proposed remedy would result in considerable and specific hardship to this witness, whose necessary mode of travel to The Hague renders it a particular hardship to go back and forth. A far more appropriate remedy that the Court has cited previously is to recall the witness if and when the accused could ever establish sufficient cause for the need to do so. And finally I would note with respect to the request for additional time for interview, of course we've always left that up to witnesses and that remains the case. However, there is no reason why the accused could not have been prepared at the time of the interview that's already taken place to ask questions based on the material that he had, indeed, already received. So with respect to all aspects of the motion, Mr. President, we submit that it is groundless and should be denied.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Tieger. Do you wish to reply, Mr. Robinson?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, very briefly. It's true we received the notification of the identity of witness KDZ-532 last Wednesday evening, on 21 September. But there was no information that made any connection with that witness to the one that was being called this week, and so we received this as delayed disclosure evidence, we put it aside -- we actually assigned it to someone to start reviewing and had no idea that this would be, until actually -- until this morning, I didn't learn of any connection between these two witnesses. And once we did see the connection, then it seemed as if we would need time to review this material, which is 371 pages, before cross-examining Witness KDZ-492. It's difficult in public session to be a little more specific so if you don't mind if we could go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The Chamber will consider the matter and issue the ruling in due course. The hearing is now adjourned. We will resume tomorrow in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 28th day of September, 2011, at 2.15 p.m. 19 20 21 22 23 24 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 7.01 p.m.,
